newsitem.title: GERMANY: DHL sees 13 pct rise in German 96 turnover.
newsitem.headline: DHL sees 13 pct rise in German 96 turnover.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express GmbH, the Germany division of DHL International, said it expected to record double-figure growth in sales revenue and consignments in 1996.
Ulrich Hartmann, DHL managing director Germany, said DHL would generate turnover of 350-360 million marks in Germany in 1996, a rise of about 13 percent on 1995.
"But this growth in turnover will not be so good as the growth in volume," he told Reuters in an interview.
DHL would export up to 4.3 million packages and documents from Germany this year, a rise of 15 percent on 1995, and handle about 4.7 million import consignments, he said.
Hartmann said the slower turnover growth could reflect pressure on prices but also more frequent usage of services.
"There is growing competition (and) there is certainly a price fall," he added.
Business had picked up in the second half of the year after growth of only two to three percent over the first six months of 1996, Hartmann said.
Express traffic from Germany to Europe was rising strongly and faster than to intercontinental destinations, although these remained the largest markets, he added.
Within Europe, Britain, Sweden and France were the major growth markets, Hartmann said.
"Clients are deciding not so much on distance as on quality. They have decided on a system and also use it over short distances," he noted.
Hartmann said DHL had a 50 to 60 percent share of the German integrators market, although each player defined the express and parcels markets slightly differently.
"The market share is relatively stable and is not growing particularly. We are growing slightly more than our competitors," he said.
"TNT and UPS are our strongest competitors," he added.
